title: Lemminkainen's Mother
text:
Lemminkainen, a reckless and boastful young hero, went to the cold northern land of Pohjola to win a bride. To earn her, he was given dangerous tasks, the last of which was to shoot the swan of Tuonela, the river of the dead. On its bank an old blind cowherd, whom he had once insulted, was waiting for him. He struck Lemminkainen with a water snake, and the young man fell into the river. The son of Tuoni, god of the dead, cut his body into pieces and threw them into the black water.

At home, Lemminkainen had left a comb with his mother, saying that if it ever began to bleed, misfortune had come to him. One day blood dripped from the comb. His mother set off at once, searching across the world, asking the trees, the road and the moon. At last the sun told her where her son lay.

She had the smith Ilmarinen forge her a huge copper rake with a long handle. She waded into the river of death and raked it again and again, bringing up his shirt, his stockings, his hat, and then piece after piece of his body. She fitted them together, bone to bone, vein to vein, and sang charms over them.

Still he lay lifeless. She sent a bee to fetch magical honey from beyond the ninth heaven and anointed him with it. Lemminkainen woke. His mother led him home.
lesson: A parent's love can be more stubborn than any danger. Even when a child brings trouble on himself, the persistence of those who love him can bring him back.
people: Lemminkainen, his mother, the blind cowherd, Ilmarinen
source: Elias Lonnrot, Kalevala (1849 edition), Runos 14 and 15
